points.label: Arrival and reception
points.left: Thessalonica and Berea receive the message differently. Acts 17:1–15 belongs to Council and the second journey.
points.right: Paul recalls boldness, work, gentleness, and fatherly appeal. 1 Thessalonians 2:1–12 belongs to Communities, suffering, and final charge.

points.label: Labor, opposition, and absence
points.left: Thessalonica and Berea receive the message differently. Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue. But those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens. Receiving a commandment to Silas and Timothy that they should come to him very quickly, they departed.
points.right: Paul recalls boldness, work, gentleness, and fatherly appeal. For you yourselves know, brothers, our visit to you wasn’t in vain, to the end that you should walk worthily of God, who calls you into his own Kingdom and glory.

payload.posture: Inspect what each source actually says before relating their chronology, argument, or remembered scene.
